newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY WEAKENS VS BASKET, ONE-DAY DEPOS JUST DOWN.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY WEAKENS VS BASKET, ONE-DAY DEPOS JUST DOWN.

text.p: The Polish zloty fell against the currency basket on importers orders and banks' closing short positions after Wednesday's central bank intervention, dealers said.
They said the zloty eased because players were keen to buy the rising mark but reluctant to part with dollars, which they wanted to keep to cover short positions carried over from yesterday.
"There was mark buying for zlotys with the dollar/zloty stable, which pushed the zloty down against the basket," said Karol Zaluski from ING Bank.

The zloty closed at 2.89/2.85 percent from the parity rate, weaker than Wednesday's 3.03/2.87 percent. It closed at 3.0710/20 to the dollar, up from 3.0730/80 on Wednesday and at 1.8330/39 to the mark, down from 1.8260/90.
Dealers did not expect significant rate moves on the local market in the near-term, as the market would stay cautious after the Wednedsay cental bank interventions against the zloty.
"Generally this was a peacefull day with thin trade -- a usual phenomenon after NBP interventions," ING's Zaluski said.

The money market focused on another increase in the maximum 14-day revrepo rate to 22.15 percent, after it rose to 22.10 on Wednesday from 21.65 percent. The seven day reverse repo rate also rose to 22.10 percent from 21.63.
Analysts said this was aimed at curbing too fast credit growth, cooling down the economy and diminishing the trade gap.
In the January-March 10 period credit for the non-financial sector rose 6.5 percent while deposits 2.2 percent. In the same period last year credit rose 3.9 percent while deposits rose 7.4 percent.
One-day deposit rates traded lower, but still well above the central bank drainage rates, as the system was squeezed by monthly tax payments.
Overnight deposit rates were at 22.35/22.55 percent, down from opening's 22.45/22.60 percent, tomorrow/next rates were at 22.35/22.55 percent, down from 22.45/22.65 percent.
